page.layout: One printed page. At the top: page number at left, running head centred. Below that: two round portrait medallions side by side, with legends around their rims. Below them: one full-width text column with two paragraphs, the first on Henry VIII and the second on Edward VI. No margin notes. No catchword or signature.

main_text.p: HENRICVS octauus, Angliæ Rex, patri Henrico septimo successit in Regno, anno Christi 1510. Qui traiecto in Galliam exercitu, Neruiorum vrbem Tornacum certis conditionibus recepit: quam quinque post annis Francisco Valesio Regi restituit, pactus filiæ suæ Mariæ connubium, cum Francisco Franciæ Delphino. Postea vero anno 1520. in Galliam reuersus visendi gratia Regis Francisci, pacem cum eo firmauit. Tragœdias vero turbulētissimas[?] quas excitauit, quásque[?] sævitias exercuit, & in Clerum, & in suas vxores, nunc commemorare non libet: qui fusius hæc videre volet, legat Iouij primum, & secundum tomum, & Supplementum Chronicorum. Regnauit annos 36. & mortuus est anno 1546.

EDVARDVS sextus, Angliæ Rex supradicti Henrici filius, annos natus octo patri successit, anno mundi 5508. & à Christo nato 1546. Hic puer fuisse dicitur (quantum tulit ætas) multum eruditus, ac pius: pacis amantissimus, & animo ad tranquillitatem inclinato. Bononiam maritimam Henrico 2. Regi Franciæ reddidit, annos quinque prius occupatâ à patre Henrico octauo. Inter eos denique post grauissima bella de pace conuentum[?] est, iis legibus, vt odiorum veterum inter Gallos, & Britannos[?] perpetua fieret amnestia: idque omnium Magnatum consensu, & populi diutinorum bellorum vtrinque pertæsi. Quasanè[?] pax, & concordia omnibus fuit quàm gratissima. Vide Chronica Franciæ[?], & Iouium.

page.notes: The medallion legends are printed on the woodcut, not in the text. The left one reads roughly "HENRIC[?] ANG. R."; a small "P G" also appears on the left medallion, faint. The right medallion reads "D. ADOAR" and "R. ANG.". Letters on the rims are partly worn; I have marked the doubtful parts with [?]. The lower part of the second paragraph is faint and blurred (around "conuentum", "Britannos", "Quasanè", "Vide Chronica"), so those readings are doubtful. The first word of the second paragraph and the numbers 1510, 1520, 5508 and 1546 were read with some care because the type is worn.
